rationale:
Split. Formalized, the supplied proof is about 450 lines of Lean. It falls into four independent, reusable obligations.

(1) A localization principle for an arbitrary measure on ℝ^P (parent step 1): an a.e. statement on A follows from the same statement on every A ∩ B_r(y) with B̄_r(y) ⊆ U.
(2) The Lebesgue differentiation theorem along closed balls for finite measures on ℝ^P (step 4(b)).
(3) The measure-theoretic part (steps 2–4 and 6(iii)). Take the finite weighted measures ν_i = (H⌞(M_i∩K)).withDensity θ_i⁺. Their Lebesgue-point limit for g = 1_A θ₂/θ₁ and the Besicovitch density of A hold H⌞(A ∩ B_r(y))-a.e. On small balls, both limits are rewritten as H-integrals.
(4) The deterministic estimate at a single point x (steps 5–8), derived from these two limits.

The selected statement then follows directly:
- Apply (1) with A = M₁ ∩ M₂ and Φ the conclusion.
- For each closed ball B̄_r(y) ⊆ U, which is compact, the hypothesis gives integrability of θ_i on M_i ∩ B̄_r(y). Apply (3) there.
- At each a.e. x ∈ A ∩ B_r(y), apply (4) with ρ = r − dist(x, y).

subproblems.title: Countable ball localization of almost-everywhere properties
subproblems.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ, let μ be any measure on ℝ^P, let U ⊆ ℝ^P be open, let A ⊆ U, and let Φ be any predicate on ℝ^P. Suppose that for all y ∈ ℝ^P and r ∈ ℝ with B̄_r(y) ⊆ U, Φ(x) holds for μ⌞(A ∩ B_r(y))-almost every x. Then Φ(x) holds for μ⌞A-almost every x.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (μ : Measure (Eucl P)) (U A : Set (Eucl P)) (Φ : Eucl P → Prop), IsOpen U → A ⊆ U → (∀ (y : Eucl P) (r : ℝ), closedBall y r ⊆ U → ∀ᵐ x ∂(μ.restrict (A ∩ ball y r)), Φ x) → ∀ᵐ x ∂(μ.restrict A), Φ x
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 1 of the parent-supplied proof (reduction to balls), stated for an arbitrary measure μ and an arbitrary predicate Φ.

1. Let ι be the type of pairs i = (y, r) ∈ ℝ^P × ℝ with B̄_r(y) ⊆ U (closedBall y r ⊆ U). For i = (y, r) ∈ ι let V_i := B_r(y) = ball y r, an open set (isOpen_ball).
2. ℝ^P = Eucl P is second countable. By TopologicalSpace.isOpen_iUnion_countable applied to the family (V_i)_{i∈ι}, there is a countable set T ⊆ ι with ⋃_{i∈T} V_i = ⋃_{i∈ι} V_i.
3. A ⊆ ⋃_{i∈T} V_i. Let x ∈ A. Then x ∈ U, and since U is open there is δ > 0 with B_δ(x) ⊆ U (Metric.isOpen_iff). The pair (x, δ/2) lies in ι because B̄_{δ/2}(x) ⊆ B_δ(x) ⊆ U (closedBall_subset_ball, as δ/2 < δ). Also x ∈ B_{δ/2}(x) because δ/2 > 0 (mem_ball_self). Hence x ∈ ⋃_{i∈ι} V_i = ⋃_{i∈T} V_i by step 2.
4. By step 3, A = A ∩ ⋃_{i∈T} V_i = ⋃_{i∈T} (A ∩ V_i) (Set.inter_eq_left, Set.inter_iUnion₂).
5. Rewrite μ⌞A as μ⌞(⋃_{i∈T} (A ∩ V_i)). T is countable, so ae_restrict_biUnion_iff applies; it requires no measurability of the sets. It shows that Φ holds μ⌞A-a.e. if and only if, for every i = (y, r) ∈ T, Φ holds μ⌞(A ∩ B_r(y))-a.e. For such i, B̄_r(y) ⊆ U because i ∈ ι, so the hypothesis gives exactly this. Hence Φ(x) holds for μ⌞A-almost every x. ∎
proof_key_steps: Index the balls B_r(y) with B̄_r(y) ⊆ U and extract a countable subfamily T with the same union (TopologicalSpace.isOpen_iUnion_countable).
Each x ∈ A ⊆ U lies in B_{δ/2}(x) with B̄_{δ/2}(x) ⊆ B_δ(x) ⊆ U, so A = ⋃_{i∈T} (A ∩ B_{r_i}(y_i)).
ae_restrict_biUnion_iff over the countable T reduces μ⌞A-a.e. Φ to the hypothesis on each A ∩ B_r(y).

subproblems.title: Lebesgue differentiation along closed balls for finite measures on ℝ^P
subproblems.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ, let ν be a finite Borel measure on ℝ^P, and let g : ℝ^P → ℝ be ν-integrable. Then for ν-almost every x, (∫⁻_{B̄_s(x)} ‖g(z) − g(x)‖ₑ dν(z)) / ν(B̄_s(x)) → 0 in [0, ∞] as s → 0⁺.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (ν : Measure (Eucl P)) [IsFiniteMeasure ν] (g : Eucl P → ℝ), Integrable g ν → ∀ᵐ x ∂ν, Tendsto (fun s : ℝ => (∫⁻ z in closedBall x s, ‖g z - g x‖ₑ ∂ν) / ν (closedBall x s)) (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 0)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 4(b) of the parent-supplied proof (Lebesgue differentiation theorem along closed balls).

1. ℝ^P = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin P) is a finite-dimensional real normed space. It is therefore a second-countable metric space carrying its Borel σ-algebra, and it has the Besicovitch covering property (instance instHasBesicovitchCovering in MeasureTheory/Covering/BesicovitchVectorSpace.lean). The finite measure ν is s-finite and locally finite (IsFiniteMeasure.toIsLocallyFiniteMeasure).
2. Consequently Besicovitch.vitaliFamily ν is a Vitali family for ν; its sets at x are the closed balls B̄_s(x) with s > 0. Besicovitch.tendsto_filterAt ν x states that s ↦ B̄_s(x) tends to the filter (Besicovitch.vitaliFamily ν).filterAt x as s → 0⁺ (along 𝓝[>] 0).
3. Since g is ν-integrable, it is locally integrable (Integrable.locallyIntegrable). Apply the Lebesgue differentiation theorem along a Vitali family, VitaliFamily.ae_tendsto_lintegral_enorm_sub_div, to Besicovitch.vitaliFamily ν. It gives, for ν-a.e. x, (∫⁻_a ‖g(z) − g(x)‖ₑ dν(z)) / ν(a) → 0 as a shrinks to x along filterAt x.
4. For each such x, compose the convergence of step 3 with the convergence of step 2 (Tendsto.comp). This gives (∫⁻_{B̄_s(x)} ‖g(z) − g(x)‖ₑ dν(z)) / ν(B̄_s(x)) → 0 as s → 0⁺. This holds for ν-a.e. x (filter_upwards), which is the claim. ∎
proof_key_steps: ℝ^P has the Besicovitch covering property, and the finite measure ν is s-finite and locally finite, so Besicovitch.vitaliFamily ν (closed balls) is a Vitali family.
Lebesgue differentiation along the Vitali family (VitaliFamily.ae_tendsto_lintegral_enorm_sub_div) applies to the locally integrable g.
Compose with Besicovitch.tendsto_filterAt ν x (s ↦ B̄_s(x) as s → 0⁺) to get the closed-ball limit ν-a.e.

subproblems.title: Weighted Lebesgue-point and Besicovitch-density limits as H-integrals, a.e. on M₁ ∩ M₂ ∩ B_r(y)
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (M₁ M₂ : Set (Eucl P)) (θ₁ θ₂ : Eucl P → ℝ) (y : Eucl P) (r : ℝ), NullMeasurableSet M₁ (μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl P)) → NullMeasurableSet M₂ (μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl P)) → (∀ z ∈ M₁, 0 < θ₁ z) → (∀ z ∈ M₂, 0 < θ₂ z) → IntegrableOn θ₁ (M₁ ∩ closedBall y r) (μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl P)) → IntegrableOn θ₂ (M₂ ∩ closedBall y r) (μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl P)) → ∀ᵐ x ∂((μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl P)).restrict (M₁ ∩ M₂ ∩ ball y r)), Tendsto (fun s : ℝ => (∫⁻ z in M₁ ∩ closedBall x s, ENNReal.ofReal (θ₁ z) * ‖(M₁ ∩ M₂).indicator (fun w => θ₂ w / θ₁ w) z - θ₂ x / θ₁ x‖ₑ ∂(μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl P))) / (∫⁻ z in M₁ ∩ closedBall x s, ENNReal.ofReal (θ₁ z) ∂(μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl P)))) (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 0) ∧ Tendsto (fun s : ℝ => (∫⁻ z in M₁ ∩ M₂ ∩ closedBall x s, ENNReal.ofReal (θ₂ z) ∂(μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl P))) / (∫⁻ z in M₂ ∩ closedBall x s, ENNReal.ofReal (θ₂ z) ∂(μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl P)))) (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 1)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: steps 2, 3, 4 and 6(iii) of the parent-supplied proof, with the ν-quantities converted to H-integrals on small balls.

Notation: H := μHE[n], A := M₁ ∩ M₂, K := B̄_r(y) = closedBall y r, B_s := B̄_s(x) = closedBall x s, t⁺ := ENNReal.ofReal t, g := A.indicator (w ↦ θ₂(w)/θ₁(w)) and λ := H⌞(A ∩ B_r(y)). For i = 1, 2 let ν_i := (H⌞(M_i ∩ K)).withDensity (z ↦ θ_i(z)⁺).

1. Finiteness. ν_i(ℝ^P) = ∫⁻_{M_i∩K} θ_i⁺ dH ≤ ∫⁻_{M_i∩K} ‖θ_i‖ₑ dH < ∞, by Real.ofReal_le_enorm and the integrability of θ_i on M_i ∩ K. So ν_i is a finite measure (isFiniteMeasure_withDensity_ofReal applied to the HasFiniteIntegral part of the hypothesis), hence s-finite and locally finite.

2. Reverse absolute continuity. M_i ∩ K is H-null-measurable, since K is closed. θ_i⁺ is AEMeasurable for H⌞(M_i∩K): take the AEStronglyMeasurable part of the integrability and apply AEMeasurable.ennreal_ofReal. For H⌞(M_i∩K)-a.e. z we have z ∈ M_i ∩ K (ae_restrict_mem₀), so θ_i(z) > 0 and θ_i(z)⁺ ≠ 0 (ENNReal.ofReal_pos). By withDensity_absolutelyContinuous', H⌞(M_i∩K) ≪ ν_i.

3. Absolute continuity of λ.
(a) A ∩ B_r(y) ⊆ M₁ ∩ K, because A ⊆ M₁ and ball y r ⊆ closedBall y r. So λ ≤ H⌞(M₁∩K) (Measure.restrict_mono), hence λ ≪ ν₁ (Measure.absolutelyContinuous_of_le, then step 2 and AbsolutelyContinuous.trans).
(b) A is null-measurable for H⌞(M₂∩K) (NullMeasurableSet.mono with Measure.restrict_le_self), so (H⌞(M₂∩K))⌞A = H⌞(A ∩ (M₂∩K)) (Measure.restrict_restrict₀). Since A ∩ B_r(y) ⊆ A ∩ (M₂∩K), we get λ ≤ (H⌞(M₂∩K))⌞A. By step 2 and AbsolutelyContinuous.restrict, (H⌞(M₂∩K))⌞A ≪ ν₂⌞A, so λ ≪ ν₂⌞A.

4. g ∈ L¹(ν₁).
(a) Measurability. A is null-measurable for H⌞(M₁∩K), and (H⌞(M₁∩K))⌞A = H⌞(A ∩ (M₁∩K)). The set A ∩ (M₁∩K) is contained in both M₂ ∩ K and M₁ ∩ K. So θ₂ and θ₁ are AEStronglyMeasurable for H⌞(A ∩ (M₁∩K)) (IntegrableOn.mono_set), and hence so is θ₂/θ₁ (AEStronglyMeasurable.div₀). By aestronglyMeasurable_indicator_iff₀, g is AEStronglyMeasurable for H⌞(M₁∩K). It is therefore also AEStronglyMeasurable for ν₁ (AEStronglyMeasurable.mono_ac, using ν₁ ≪ H⌞(M₁∩K) from withDensity_absolutelyContinuous).
(b) Finite integral. θ₁⁺ and ‖g‖ₑ are AEMeasurable for H⌞(M₁∩K), so lintegral_withDensity_eq_lintegral_mul₀ gives ∫⁻ ‖g‖ₑ dν₁ = ∫⁻ θ₁⁺·‖g‖ₑ d(H⌞(M₁∩K)). Pointwise, θ₁⁺·‖g‖ₑ = A.indicator θ₂⁺:
- If z ∈ A, then θ₁(z), θ₂(z) > 0 and θ₁(z)⁺·‖θ₂(z)/θ₁(z)‖ₑ = (θ₁(z)·(θ₂(z)/θ₁(z)))⁺ = θ₂(z)⁺ (Real.enorm_of_nonneg, ENNReal.ofReal_mul, mul_div_cancel₀).
- If z ∉ A, then g(z) = 0 and both sides are 0.
Hence ∫⁻ ‖g‖ₑ dν₁ = ∫⁻_{A∩(M₁∩K)} θ₂⁺ dH (lintegral_indicator₀, Measure.restrict_restrict₀). This is ≤ ∫⁻_{M₂∩K} θ₂⁺ dH (lintegral_mono_set), which is ≤ ∫⁻_{M₂∩K} ‖θ₂‖ₑ dH < ∞. Thus g is integrable for ν₁.

5. A.e. differentiation.
(a) Apply the sibling lemma fiw_tl_ald_closedBall_lebesgue_point (Lebesgue differentiation along closed balls) to the finite measure ν₁ and g ∈ L¹(ν₁). For ν₁-a.e. x, Q₁(s) := (∫⁻_{B_s} ‖g(z) − g(x)‖ₑ dν₁(z)) / ν₁(B_s) → 0 as s → 0⁺. By 3(a) and AbsolutelyContinuous.ae_le, this holds for λ-a.e. x.
(b) Apply the Besicovitch density theorem Besicovitch.ae_tendsto_measure_inter_div ν₂ A. Its hypotheses hold: ν₂ is locally finite and ℝ^P has the Besicovitch covering property. For ν₂⌞A-a.e. x, Q₂(s) := ν₂(A ∩ B_s) / ν₂(B_s) → 1 as s → 0⁺. By 3(b), this holds for λ-a.e. x.
(c) For λ-a.e. x, x ∈ A ∩ B_r(y) (ae_restrict_mem₀; A ∩ B_r(y) is H-null-measurable).
Fix x satisfying (a), (b) and (c) (filter_upwards). It remains to prove (L) and (D) at x.

6. Identification on small balls. Since x ∈ B_r(y), ρ := r − dist(x, y) > 0, and the interval (0, ρ) belongs to 𝓝[>] 0 (Ioo_mem_nhdsGT). For s ∈ (0, ρ), B_s ⊆ K by closedBall_subset_closedBall', since s + dist(x, y) ≤ r. Hence B_s ∩ (M_i∩K) = M_i ∩ B_s, and (A ∩ B_s) ∩ (M₂∩K) = A ∩ B_s because A ⊆ M₂. Since B_s is measurable:
(i) ν_i(B_s) = ∫⁻_{B_s} θ_i⁺ d(H⌞(M_i∩K)) = ∫⁻_{M_i∩B_s} θ_i⁺ dH (withDensity_apply with measurableSet_closedBall, then Measure.restrict_restrict).
(ii) ∫⁻_{B_s} ‖g − g(x)‖ₑ dν₁ = ∫⁻_{B_s} θ₁⁺·‖g − g(x)‖ₑ d(H⌞(M₁∩K)) = ∫⁻_{M₁∩B_s} θ₁⁺·‖g − g(x)‖ₑ dH. This uses setLIntegral_withDensity_eq_lintegral_mul₀ (θ₁⁺ and ‖g − g(x)‖ₑ are AEMeasurable for H⌞(M₁∩K) by 4(a)) and Measure.restrict_restrict. Moreover g(x) = θ₂(x)/θ₁(x) because x ∈ A (Set.indicator_of_mem).
(iii) ν₂(A ∩ B_s) = ∫⁻_{A∩B_s} θ₂⁺ d(H⌞(M₂∩K)) = ∫⁻_{A∩B_s} θ₂⁺ dH. This uses withDensity_apply₀ (A ∩ B_s is null-measurable for H⌞(M₂∩K)) and Measure.restrict_restrict₀.
So for every s ∈ (0, ρ), Q₁(s) equals the ratio in (L) and Q₂(s) equals the ratio in (D); note that A ∩ B_s is the Lean set M₁ ∩ M₂ ∩ closedBall x s. The functions agree eventually along 𝓝[>] 0, so Tendsto.congr' transfers the limits of 5(a) and 5(b): (L) and (D) hold at x. This is true for λ-almost every x. ∎
proof_key_steps: ν_i := (H⌞(M_i∩K)).withDensity θ_i⁺ with K = B̄_r(y) is finite, and H⌞(M_i∩K) ≪ ν_i because θ_i > 0 on M_i (withDensity_absolutelyContinuous').
λ = H⌞(A ∩ B_r(y)) satisfies λ ≤ H⌞(M₁∩K) ≪ ν₁ and λ ≤ (H⌞(M₂∩K))⌞A ≪ ν₂⌞A.
g = 1_A θ₂/θ₁ is in L¹(ν₁), since θ₁⁺‖g‖ₑ = 1_A θ₂⁺ and θ₂ is integrable on M₂ ∩ K.
The sibling Lebesgue-point lemma for (ν₁, g) and Besicovitch.ae_tendsto_measure_inter_div for (ν₂, A) hold λ-a.e., as does x ∈ A ∩ B_r(y).
For 0 < s < r − dist(x, y), B̄_s(x) ⊆ K, the ν-ratios equal the H-ratios in (L) and (D), and g(x) = θ₂(x)/θ₁(x); conclude by Tendsto.congr'.

subproblems.title: Relative L¹ estimate at a point from the Lebesgue-point and density limits
subproblems.statement:
Let P, n ∈ ℕ and H := μHE[n] on ℝ^P. Let M₁, M₂ ⊆ ℝ^P be H-null-measurable, let θ₁, θ₂ : ℝ^P → ℝ with θ_i > 0 on M_i, and let x ∈ M₁ ∩ M₂. Assume there is ρ > 0 such that θ_i is H-integrable on M_i ∩ B̄_ρ(x) (i = 1, 2). Put A := M₁ ∩ M₂, g := 1_A·(θ₂/θ₁) and c := θ₂(x)/θ₁(x). Assume that as s → 0⁺ (quotients in [0, ∞]):
(L) (∫⁻_{M₁∩B̄_s(x)} ofReal(θ₁)·‖g − c‖ₑ dH) / (∫⁻_{M₁∩B̄_s(x)} ofReal(θ₁) dH) → 0;
(D) (∫⁻_{A∩B̄_s(x)} ofReal(θ₂) dH) / (∫⁻_{M₂∩B̄_s(x)} ofReal(θ₂) dH) → 1.
Then for every ε > 0 and all sufficiently small s > 0, ∫⁻_{B̄_s(x)} ‖1_{M₂}θ₂ − c·1_{M₁}θ₁‖ₑ dH ≤ ofReal(ε)·∫⁻_{M₁∩B̄_s(x)} ofReal(θ₁) dH.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (M₁ M₂ : Set (Eucl P)) (θ₁ θ₂ : Eucl P → ℝ) (x : Eucl P), NullMeasurableSet M₁ (μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl P)) → NullMeasurableSet M₂ (μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl P)) → (∀ z ∈ M₁, 0 < θ₁ z) → (∀ z ∈ M₂, 0 < θ₂ z) → x ∈ M₁ ∩ M₂ → (∃ ρ : ℝ, 0 < ρ ∧ IntegrableOn θ₁ (M₁ ∩ closedBall x ρ) (μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl P)) ∧ IntegrableOn θ₂ (M₂ ∩ closedBall x ρ) (μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl P))) → Tendsto (fun s : ℝ => (∫⁻ z in M₁ ∩ closedBall x s, ENNReal.ofReal (θ₁ z) * ‖(M₁ ∩ M₂).indicator (fun w => θ₂ w / θ₁ w) z - θ₂ x / θ₁ x‖ₑ ∂(μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl P))) / (∫⁻ z in M₁ ∩ closedBall x s, ENNReal.ofReal (θ₁ z) ∂(μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl P)))) (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 0) → Tendsto (fun s : ℝ => (∫⁻ z in M₁ ∩ M₂ ∩ closedBall x s, ENNReal.ofReal (θ₂ z) ∂(μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl P))) / (∫⁻ z in M₂ ∩ closedBall x s, ENNReal.ofReal (θ₂ z) ∂(μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl P)))) (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 1) → ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∀ᶠ s in 𝓝[>] (0 : ℝ), ∫⁻ z in closedBall x s, ‖M₂.indicator θ₂ z - θ₂ x / θ₁ x * M₁.indicator θ₁ z‖ₑ ∂(μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl P)) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal ε * ∫⁻ z in M₁ ∩ closedBall x s, ENNReal.ofReal (θ₁ z) ∂(μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl P))
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: steps 5–8 of the parent-supplied proof, with the ν-quantities written as H-integrals.

Notation: H := μHE[n], A := M₁ ∩ M₂, c := θ₂(x)/θ₁(x), g := A.indicator (w ↦ θ₂(w)/θ₁(w)), t⁺ := ENNReal.ofReal t and B_s := closedBall x s. For s > 0 put:
- b₁(s) := ∫⁻_{M₁∩B_s} θ₁⁺ dH and I(s) := ∫⁻_{M₁∩B_s} θ₁⁺·‖g − c‖ₑ dH;
- a₂(s) := ∫⁻_{A∩B_s} θ₂⁺ dH, b₂(s) := ∫⁻_{M₂∩B_s} θ₂⁺ dH and d₂(s) := ∫⁻_{(M₂∖M₁)∩B_s} θ₂⁺ dH.
The hypotheses say (L) I(s)/b₁(s) → 0 and (D) a₂(s)/b₂(s) → 1 as s → 0⁺, and θ_i is integrable on M_i ∩ B̄_ρ(x).

1. Constants. x ∈ M₁ ∩ M₂ gives θ₁(x), θ₂(x) > 0, so c > 0. Fix ε > 0 and put δ := min(1/2, ε/(3c + 3)). Then 0 < δ ≤ 1/2, and δ(3c + 3) ≤ ε (min_le_right, le_div_iff₀).

2. Eventual conditions. Each of the following holds for all s in a set belonging to 𝓝[>] 0; combine them with filter_upwards.
(E1) s ∈ (0, ρ) (Ioo_mem_nhdsGT). Then B_s ⊆ B̄_ρ(x) (closedBall_subset_closedBall), so θ_i is integrable on M_i ∩ B_s (IntegrableOn.mono_set).
(E2) (1 − δ)⁺ < a₂(s)/b₂(s). This follows from (D) via (tendsto_order.1 (D)).1, because (1 − δ)⁺ < 1 (ENNReal.ofReal_lt_one, δ > 0).
(E3) I(s)/b₁(s) < δ⁺. This follows from (L) via (tendsto_order.1 (L)).2, because δ⁺ > 0 (ENNReal.ofReal_pos).
Fix such an s, write B := B_s and b₁ := b₁(s), etc. It suffices to prove ∫⁻_B ‖M₂.indicator θ₂ − c·M₁.indicator θ₁‖ₑ dH ≤ ε⁺·b₁.

3. Finiteness. By (E1), b₁ < ∞ and b₂ < ∞ (IntegrableOn.setLIntegral_lt_top).

4. Splitting and the two limits.
(i) b₂ = a₂ + d₂. Split H⌞(M₂∩B) along the H-null-measurable set M₁: H⌞((M₂∩B) ∩ M₁) + H⌞((M₂∩B)∖M₁) = H⌞(M₂∩B) (Measure.restrict_inter_add_sdiff₀). Then integrate (lintegral_add_measure), using (M₂∩B) ∩ M₁ = A ∩ B and (M₂∩B)∖M₁ = (M₂∖M₁) ∩ B.
(ii) (1 − δ)⁺·b₂ ≤ a₂. This follows from (E2) by ENNReal.lt_div_iff_mul_lt. Its side conditions b₂ ≠ 0 ∨ (1 − δ)⁺ ≠ ∞ and b₂ ≠ ∞ ∨ (1 − δ)⁺ ≠ 0 hold because (1 − δ)⁺ ≠ ∞ and b₂ ≠ ∞.
(iii) I ≤ δ⁺·b₁. This is trivial if I = 0. Otherwise (E3) and ENNReal.div_lt_iff give I < δ⁺·b₁; the side conditions b₁ ≠ 0 ∨ I ≠ 0 and b₁ ≠ ∞ ∨ I ≠ ∞ hold since I ≠ 0 and b₁ ≠ ∞.

5. a₂ ≤ c⁺·b₁ + I. Let z ∈ A. Then θ₁(z) > 0 and g(z) = θ₂(z)/θ₁(z), so θ₂(z) = cθ₁(z) + θ₁(z)(g(z) − c) ≤ cθ₁(z) + θ₁(z)|g(z) − c|. Hence θ₂(z)⁺ ≤ c⁺θ₁(z)⁺ + θ₁(z)⁺‖g(z) − c‖ₑ (Real.enorm_eq_ofReal_abs, ENNReal.ofReal_mul, ENNReal.ofReal_add, ENNReal.ofReal_le_ofReal).
A ∩ B is H-null-measurable, so this bound holds H⌞(A∩B)-a.e. (ae_restrict_mem₀). By lintegral_mono_ae, a₂ ≤ ∫⁻_{A∩B} (c⁺θ₁⁺ + θ₁⁺‖g − c‖ₑ) dH. Next enlarge A ∩ B to M₁ ∩ B (lintegral_mono_set). Split the sum with lintegral_add_left'; this is allowed because c⁺θ₁⁺ is AEMeasurable for H⌞(M₁∩B) by (E1). Finally pull out the constant c⁺ ≠ ∞ (lintegral_const_mul'). This gives a₂ ≤ c⁺·b₁ + I.

6. Pointwise decomposition. For every z ∈ ℝ^P,
‖M₂.indicator θ₂ z − c·M₁.indicator θ₁ z‖ₑ ≤ M₁.indicator (θ₁⁺·‖g − c‖ₑ) z + (M₂∖M₁).indicator θ₂⁺ z.
Check by cases:
- z ∈ M₁ ∩ M₂: θ₂(z) − cθ₁(z) = θ₁(z)·(θ₂(z)/θ₁(z) − c), so the left side equals θ₁(z)⁺‖g(z) − c‖ₑ (enorm_mul, Real.enorm_eq_ofReal with θ₁(z) ≥ 0). This is the first term on the right.
- z ∈ M₁∖M₂: g(z) = 0 and 0 − cθ₁(z) = θ₁(z)(0 − c), so the left side again equals the first term.
- z ∈ M₂∖M₁: the left side is ‖θ₂(z)‖ₑ = θ₂(z)⁺ (θ₂(z) > 0), which is the second term.
- Otherwise the left side is ‖0 − c·0‖ₑ = 0.
Integrate over B (lintegral_mono). The second summand is AEMeasurable for H⌞B. Indeed, by aemeasurable_indicator_iff₀ (M₂∖M₁ is null-measurable for H⌞B) it suffices that θ₂⁺ is AEMeasurable for (H⌞B)⌞(M₂∖M₁) = H⌞((M₂∖M₁)∩B) (Measure.restrict_restrict'). This follows from (E1), since (M₂∖M₁)∩B ⊆ M₂∩B. So lintegral_add_right' splits the integral. setLIntegral_indicator₀ identifies the two pieces: ∫⁻_B S.indicator f dH = ∫⁻_{S∩B} f dH whenever S is null-measurable for H⌞B. Therefore
∫⁻_B ‖M₂.indicator θ₂ − c·M₁.indicator θ₁‖ₑ dH ≤ I + d₂.

7. Arithmetic. The quantities b₁, b₂, a₂ ≤ b₂, d₂ ≤ b₂ and I ≤ δ⁺b₁ are all finite. So we may pass to real parts (ENNReal.toReal_mono, toReal_add, toReal_mul, toReal_ofReal). Let B₁, B₂, A₂, D₂ and J be the real parts of b₁, b₂, a₂, d₂ and I. Then:
- A₂ + D₂ ≤ B₂ (by 4(i)), (1 − δ)B₂ ≤ A₂ (by 4(ii)), J ≤ δB₁ (by 4(iii)) and A₂ ≤ cB₁ + J (by step 5).
- Hence D₂ ≤ B₂ − A₂ ≤ δB₂ and A₂ ≤ (c + δ)B₁.
- As 1 − δ ≥ 1/2, B₂ ≤ 2A₂ ≤ 2(c + δ)B₁.
- Therefore J + D₂ ≤ δB₁ + δB₂ ≤ δ(1 + 2c + 2δ)B₁ ≤ δ(3c + 3)B₁ ≤ εB₁, using 2δ ≤ 1, c ≥ 0 and B₁ ≥ 0 (linarith, nlinarith).

8. Conclusion. Let L := ∫⁻_B ‖M₂.indicator θ₂ − c·M₁.indicator θ₁‖ₑ dH. By steps 6 and 7, L ≤ I + d₂ < ∞ and L.toReal ≤ J + D₂ ≤ εB₁. Hence L = (L.toReal)⁺ ≤ (εB₁)⁺ = ε⁺·b₁ (ENNReal.ofReal_toReal, ENNReal.ofReal_le_ofReal, ENNReal.ofReal_mul with ε ≥ 0). This is the required inequality at s, with c = θ₂(x)/θ₁(x). It holds for all s in a set belonging to 𝓝[>] 0, and ε > 0 was arbitrary, so the theorem follows. ∎
proof_key_steps: c = θ₂(x)/θ₁(x) > 0 and δ = min(1/2, ε/(3c+3)). Eventually s < ρ, a₂/b₂ > (1−δ)⁺ and I/b₁ < δ⁺.
b₁ and b₂ are finite, b₂ = a₂ + d₂ (split along M₁), (1−δ)b₂ ≤ a₂ (ENNReal.lt_div_iff_mul_lt) and I ≤ δb₁ (ENNReal.div_lt_iff).
On A, θ₂ ≤ cθ₁ + θ₁|g − c|, so a₂ ≤ c·b₁ + I.
Pointwise, |1_{M₂}θ₂ − c1_{M₁}θ₁| ≤ 1_{M₁}θ₁|g − c| + 1_{M₂∖M₁}θ₂, so the integral over B̄_s(x) is at most I + d₂.
Real arithmetic: I + d₂ ≤ δb₁ + δb₂ ≤ δ(3c+3)b₁ ≤ εb₁.
